$comment: D7 — boundary_lookup's matching algorithm and speech act. Normative and machine-checkable; the prose ruling is docs/design/ADR-0007-boundary-lookup-matching-and-speech-act.md. Sits beside runtime-pin.json (D1), tool-contracts.json (D3), extraction-contract.json (D4), correctness-invariant.json (D5) and width-and-band-contract.json (D6). Every number here was measured against the live tree on the date below; nothing is asserted from memory.

gateBaseline.smoke: 26 of 27 — the pre-existing loop-v1 v1-conductor planner failure recorded in mcp/runtime-pin.json gateBaseline; unrelated to and untouched by D7
gateBaseline.gitDiffStat: only .claude/skills/loop-engine/references/execution-modes.md, from D4 and D6; D7 modified no existing file

verdict.rule: verdict is ONE prose string. The server MUST NOT parse it into fields, MUST NOT extract sentences from it as structured claims, and MUST NOT reuse the name `verdict` for any computed result field. Citing it means the single line 742..742.

drifted.delta: live adds the loop-debug clause 'or that used to be fast and is not any more … an unexplained regression is a defect, not a mechanism choice'
live adds a whole loop-ship pointer sentence absent from the approved text

citationMechanics.lineSpanRule: Brace-depth scan upward to the enclosing object's `{` line, then forward to depth 0. Measured: the loop-design matrix row is lines 111..132.
citationMechanics.excerptIsAFragment: MEASURED — the cited span ends in `},` and does NOT JSON.parse standalone. The citation is a byte range plus an RFC 6901 pointer; a caller must not treat the excerpt as a JSON document. sha256 is over the LF-normalised raw lines, per ADR-0003 D3.2.

D7_1_speechAct.rule: Every answer is an ASSERTIVE (a cited report of what boundary-audit.json says) plus a DIRECTIVE (a question the caller must answer). It is NEVER a DECLARATION — it does not make any skill the owner of anything.
why: docs/c4/README.md:33 — 'the descriptions *are* the routing table'. Selection happens on the description field before any body loads, so this tool cannot be the selector.
docs/design/README.md:7 and :20 — boundary-audit.json 'Outranks the build manifest'. A one-line owner emitted from this file's authority converts a ranking guess into a ruling.
mcp/tool-contracts.json D3.0 — authoringTimeOnly:true. The tool is unreachable from a running workflow; it advises an author, it does not route a request.
D7_1_speechAct.verdictNameIsReserved: `verdict` is the 4394-character prose string at /verdict. A computed field of that name would let a caller believe the file ruled.

minimumShortlist.limitOfOneBehaviour: If the caller passes limit:1 the server returns 2 and appends a notes[] entry naming this clause. A one-element shortlist is a verdict wearing a list's clothes.

D7_1_speechAct.authorityConstant: boundary-audit.json outranks any plan or build manifest (docs/design/README.md:7). This ranking is the server's, computed by the documented score in mcp/boundary-match-contract.json; the authority is the file's. A rank is not a ruling — read the separating question and decide.

neverScored: overlaps[].risk and overlaps[].resolution — retrieval evidence and pair discriminators, not row identity
verdict — one prose string, cited never scored

diversion.rule: A query hit inside matrix[i].useInsteadWhen[j].condition is reported as divertedBy[] on row i, naming otherSkill. It is NOT added to row i's score, and NOT added to otherSkill's score either.

measuredWhyNotOwnRow.query: plan a whole project into phases with a task DAG and per-node model routing
measuredWhyNotOwnRow.cause: /matrix/0/useInsteadWhen/0 reads 'The unit of work is a whole project needing phase decomposition, a task DAG, and per-node model/effort routing before any script is written.' -> use loop-orchestrate. The best evidence for loop-engine is a sentence that disclaims loop-engine.

diversion.measuredWhyNotTransferToTarget: An additive transfer to otherSkill widened that margin from 2.9% to 28% but demoted loop-skill from rank 1 to rank 5 on its own query, because the bonus is an in-degree popularity term and loop-skill has in-degree 0.

idf.form: IDF[d] = round(1000 * ln((2N+2)/(2d+1)))  — Robertson's probabilistic IDF, closed form, in milli-nats
idf.d: document frequency of the term over the N own-field bags (scope + approved description)
idf.outOfVocabularyRule: d = 0 takes the MAXIMUM entry (3784), not zero. An unknown query term is evidence against every row. Scoring it zero collapses the normaliser and is what produced the 1.571 off-fleet coverage in D7_4.

portability.hazard: ECMAScript does not require Math.log to be correctly rounded (implementation-approximated), so a float score is not portable — the same class ADR-0005 D5.4 ruled on for the estimator.
portability.measuredMargin: closest any of the 22 entries comes to a .5 rounding boundary = 7.735e-2; a float ulp at these magnitudes = 6.66e-13. Eleven orders of magnitude. Zero entries at risk.
portability.consequence: Math.log is evaluated exactly N+1 times, at table construction only. It never appears in the comparison path.

idf.noStopwordList: There is none, deliberately. df is measured from the corpus: a term in all 21 rows scores 23 against 2686 for a term in one — a 117x ratio. A declared stopword list would be a hand-chosen constant about what the file says, which is the class of value ADR-0005 I1 forbids.

termFrequency.why: Repeating a word must not buy proportional score. Measured: 67.8% of (term,row) pairs have tf === 1, so saturation is cheap insurance rather than a load-bearing knob.

fieldWeightingAndMissingData.renormalisation: Weights are renormalised over the fields ACTUALLY PRESENT. For the 3 rows with no approved description, scope carries weight 1 and fieldsScored records ['scope'].

noLengthNormalisation.measured: b=0.75 lifts the three description-less rows from mean rank 15.67 to 12.00 on a query none of them own (loop-skill 14->8, loop-v1 12->7). A scorer that pays a row for absent data is a silent default in ADR-0005's sense.

arithmetic.rule: BigInt rationals throughout the comparison path. No float and no Math.log at compare time.
arithmetic.measured: largest value seen was an 8-digit numerator over a 4-digit denominator; 1.453 ms/call against 1.458 ms/call for the float path.
arithmetic.equivalence: MEASURED — the exact-integer ranking reproduces the float-log ranking identically on all 21 rows for all 20 on-fleet queries.
arithmetic.displayNormaliser: The per-query 1/qmass factor is a positive constant across rows and therefore cannot change the order. It is applied ONLY to the displayed `score` (6 decimal places), never to the ordering.

ordering.totality: All three keys are total. The last is the source file's own byte order, so ties are never broken by object-key order, filesystem order or float noise.
ordering.measuredTies: 26 adjacent pairs across the 20-query set have an exact-zero score gap; all fall through to the tie-break chain.

D7_4_unowned.rule: outcome === 'unowned' IFF the top-ranked row matches fewer than MIN_DISCRIMINATING distinct DISCRIMINATING query terms. No score threshold appears anywhere in this predicate.
D7_4_unowned.discriminatingTerm: a query term t with 1 <= df(t) <= DF_MAX
D7_4_unowned.DF_MAX: floor(N/4) — 5 at N=21, read from the live matrix size

measuredScoreFloorDoesNotExist.experiment: 20 on-fleet queries (one per skill, loop-ship twice) vs 12 deliberately off-fleet queries, top candidate only

absoluteMatchedIdfMass.rejectedBecause: scales with query length; a long off-fleet query accumulates mass and crosses it

measuredScoreFloorDoesNotExist.worstFloorFailure: 'reconcile the Q3 payroll spreadsheet' scored 1.571 — the highest coverage in the whole experiment — because almost every term was out of vocabulary, the denominator collapsed, and one match on 'the' filled it.

failures: 'translate this paragraph into French' -> loop-design on {this,into}

D7_4_unowned.notATunedConstant: docs/design/README.md:12 claims the 21 scope lines are 'mutually exclusive by construction'. A term appearing in a quarter of the rows is, by that claim, not a boundary term. floor(N/4) restates the file's claim about itself and moves when a 22nd skill lands.

answerShape.neverNotFound: not_found is for an unknown KEY (D7_9). The absence of an owner is a different fact from the absence of a key; collapsing them would leave loop-v1's roster sweep unable to tell a typo from a decomposition smell.
answerShape.neverEmpty: candidates[] is still populated with the top 3, each carrying its score and its zero-or-one discriminating terms, so the caller can see HOW nothing matched. An empty array is indistinguishable from a broken parse.
answerShape.decompositionSmell: No row of the 21-skill matrix matches this ask on two or more discriminating terms. Per .claude/skills/loop-v1/SKILL.md:31, a task with no owning skill is a decomposition smell: split the task until each part has an owner, or record deliberately that it falls outside the fleet. Do not assign the highest-scoring row by default.

D7_5_bothDirections.rule: Every candidate returns BOTH its outbound edges and every inbound edge pointing at it.
law: .claude/skills/loop-skill/SKILL.md:47 — 'for every rated overlap, on *both* sides. A one-way pointer leaves the boundary decidable from one direction only.'
.claude/skills/loop-skill/references/authoring.md:69 — check the description 'against every neighbour's reciprocal pointer'
docs/design/README.md:18 — 'A description that stops encoding its half of an overlap makes that boundary one-way.'

fields.useInsteadWhen: the row's own outbound edges, VERBATIM as stored, each with pointer /matrix/{i}/useInsteadWhen/{j}
fields.pointedAtBy: SYNTHESISED by scanning all N rows for edges targeting this skill. Each entry carries the pointer to where it is ACTUALLY stored — /matrix/{k}/useInsteadWhen/{m} — so the citation is real and not invented. Each is marked direction:'inbound'.
fields.reciprocity: { outDegree, inDegree, oneWayOut[], oneWayIn[] } — per candidate

D7_5_bothDirections.measuredNecessity: 22 of 76 edges are one-way today, and loop-skill and loop-frontend have in-degree 0 — nothing in the file ever says 'use loop-skill instead'. A caller who lands on loop-design and is never told loop-frontend diverts to it has been handed a boundary that is only half decidable.
D7_5_bothDirections.cost: A full N-row scan per candidate: 441 edge comparisons at N=21, inside the 1.45 ms. At 100 skills this is the first thing to index.

D7_6_separatingQuestion.rule: For EVERY adjacent pair in the returned shortlist — not only #1/#2, and never gated on a margin band — return the stored condition verbatim as a decidable proposition with its consequence attached.

shape.margin: (score_a - score_b)/score_a, 4 decimal places, REPORTED not used as a gate

D7_6_separatingQuestion.noParaphrase: The proposition is the stored condition byte-for-byte. No model call, no rewriting, no synonym expansion, no interrogative transformation beyond the fixed ifTrue/ifFalse frame. The tool presents the file's sentence; it does not author one.

nullBranchIsRequired.rule: Where no edge exists in either direction: storedDiscriminator:false, propositions:[], plus a notes[] entry naming the gap against loop-skill/SKILL.md:47.
nullBranchIsRequired.measuredFrequency: 161 of 210 unordered pairs have no stored discriminator. On the 20-query set the #1/#2 pair had both directions on 9, one direction on 4, and NONE on 7.
nullBranchIsRequired.why: Fabricating a question for those 7 is the only genuinely dishonest act available to this tool.

marginIsNotACorrectnessSignal.conclusion: A band tight enough to be meaningful catches nothing; a band wide enough to catch the errors flags 40% of all queries. Report the margin, gate nothing on it.

theVindicatingMeasurement.query: what is in this release and how risky is it
theVindicatingMeasurement.ranking: WRONG — loop-ship 0.534, loop-audit 0.343 (margin 36%, outside any usable band)
theVindicatingMeasurement.returnedProposition: [loop-ship] 'The ask is what is in the release and how risky it is, not how it reaches production.' -> if TRUE use loop-audit
theVindicatingMeasurement.conclusion: The stored question is a near-verbatim restatement of the query. A caller who reads it gets the right answer from a wrong ranking. The ranking is a retrieval device for the question; the question is the answer.

D7_7_oneAuthorityInTheRanking.rule: The score reads descriptionRewrites[].newDescription — the APPROVED text — and never the live SKILL.md frontmatter. Blending the ruled text and the shipped text into one number makes the score a mixture of two authorities with no way to see which moved.
D7_7_oneAuthorityInTheRanking.liveTextIsStillRead: for exactly one purpose: ADR-0003's descriptionIsStale.

requiredChangeToD3.why: A boolean cannot honestly describe the 3 rows with no approved text. `false` there asserts 'the live text matches what was approved' when nothing was approved — a silent default in ADR-0005's sense.
requiredChangeToD3.notApplied: tool-contracts.json is D3's deliverable from this same phase. Queued here alongside D5's unknown_task_kind and D6's width_undetermined / mode_not_priceable.

D7_8_auditIntegrity.rule: Every answer carries an auditIntegrity block, computed LIVE from the file, never hardcoded.
D7_8_auditIntegrity.why: docs/design/README.md:19 says adding a skill means re-checking every overlap it touches, and :18 says a description that stops encoding its half of an overlap makes the boundary one-way. Both are currently unmet. A tool that reads the file that outranks the build manifest and reports none of this launders the debt into a confident-looking ranking.
D7_8_auditIntegrity.acceptedRisk: It will be non-zero on every call until someone repairs the file, and may become wallpaper. It is REQUIRED rather than optional precisely so a repair commit visibly zeroes it.

D7_9_exactLookup.rule: `skill:` alone is an exact key lookup. outcome:'exact'. The scorer never runs and `unowned` is never returned.
D7_9_exactLookup.absentKey: not_found per mcp/tool-contracts.json D3.5_errorEnvelope — 'boundary_lookup on a skill absent from the 21-entry matrix'
D7_9_exactLookup.why: The absence of a KEY (a typo, a renamed skill, a stale plan) is a different fact from the absence of an OWNER (a decomposition smell). loop-v1's roster sweep must be able to tell them apart.

D7_10_measuredQuality.harness: 20 on-fleet queries (one per skill, loop-ship twice) + 12 deliberately off-fleet queries, run against the live docs/design/boundary-audit.json
D7_10_measuredQuality.determinism: two identical calls return byte-identical structuredContent (19,265 bytes for a 5-candidate answer)

knownCeiling.case: 'why does this throw a null pointer on the second call' ranks loop-debug FIFTH
knownCeiling.cause: the query shares no discriminating term with an approved description written around 'a bug, a failing test, an exception or stack trace, a crash'
knownCeiling.consequence: inside limit:5, outcome still 'candidates', top entry WRONG. This is the ceiling of a no-model no-embedding design.
knownCeiling.mitigation: the speech act never claims the top entry is the owner, and the D3.8 fallback ('read docs/design/boundary-audit.json') is present in every answer

D7_11_gateAssertions: G7.1 No result field of any boundary_lookup answer is named owner / owningSkill / owns / verdict / decision / answer / winner / selected — assert by scanning the serialized structuredContent key set on every golden query.
G7.2 outcome:'candidates' implies candidates.length >= 2; limit:1 returns 2 plus the D7_1 notes[] entry.
G7.3 The 22-entry IDF table computed at load equals the tableAtN21 literal in this contract, element for element, when matrix.length === 21.

G7.4 No float appears in the comparison path: the ranking function's reachable source contains no Math.log, no Math.pow, no `/` on Numbers used for ordering — static scan, same technique as ADR-0005 G5.7.
G7.5 Determinism: the same query twice returns byte-identical structuredContent; and the ranking is invariant under shuffling the in-memory row array, since the final tie-break is the matrix index.
G7.6 The 12 off-fleet queries in D7_4 all return outcome:'unowned'; the 20 on-fleet queries all return outcome:'candidates' with the expected skill inside limit:5.
G7.7 useInsteadWhen text is not scored: assert that a query built ONLY from /matrix/0/useInsteadWhen/0's condition does not rank loop-engine above loop-orchestrate.

G7.8 For every candidate, pointedAtBy is complete — recompute the inbound edge set independently and assert set equality; and every pointedAtBy entry's pointer resolves to the asserted condition string in the file.

G7.9 Every adjacent pair in the shortlist carries a separation object; where storedDiscriminator is true every proposition string is byte-identical to the file at its pointer; where false, propositions is [] and a notes[] entry names the gap.
G7.10 A contrived query whose top-2 pair is one of the 161 pairs with no stored discriminator returns storedDiscriminator:false — assert the null branch actually executes rather than being dead code.
G7.11 auditIntegrity is computed live: plant a synthetic 22nd matrix row in a SCRATCH COPY of the tree and assert matrixSize becomes 22 and DF_MAX becomes 5 (floor(22/4)); never mutate the repo.
G7.12 descriptionIsStale returns 'unrecorded' for loop-skill, loop-frontend and loop-v1, 'drifted' for loop-algo and loop-operate, 'current' for the other 16.

G7.13 Citation round-trip (inherits ADR-0003 D3.9): every citation's sha256 recomputes over the LF-normalised line range, and the excerpt is asserted NOT to JSON.parse standalone for a matrix row, since it is a fragment.
G7.14 boundary_lookup with skill:'loop-nonexistent' returns ok:false code 'not_found' — never outcome:'unowned'.
G7.15 The verdict string is never parsed: assert no result field is derived from /verdict other than a citation whose line range is exactly 742..742.
D7_12_notRuledHere: Repairing the audit's 22 one-way edges, 9 one-way rated overlaps, 2 zero-in-degree skills, 3 missing approved descriptions, 2 drifted descriptions or loop-v1's absent overlap rows. D7 rules on the TOOL, not the file; every one of these is reported by auditIntegrity and owned by nobody.
The wording of any consumer-router edit. ADR-0003 D3.8 keys fallbacks to call sites; D7 adds outcome:'unowned', which D3.8's table has no row for.

Whether boundary_lookup should also read the live SKILL.md descriptions as a SECOND ranked corpus, since docs/c4/README.md:33 makes those the actual selector. D7 rules one authority in the ranking; a second, separately-reported ranking is a coherent future option and is not decided here.
Synonym or stem handling. The tokenizer does no stemming; 'tests' and 'testing' are distinct terms. Measured impact was not isolated.
Any change to mcp/tool-contracts.json. D7_7 specifies one edit verbatim and does not apply it.
